--- title: "Parsing and AST" guide-section: "Core Concepts" tags: [Tutorial] bread-crumbs: false --- multimark exposes the full abstract syntax tree (AST) that cmark-gfm builds during parsing. This lets you inspect document structure, extract content, transform nodes, and render subtrees. This is all backed by the same C library that powers the renderers. ## Parsing to an AST The `parse()` function takes a Markdown string and returns the root `Node` of the parsed tree. ::: {#981c3cf9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from multimark import parse, NodeType doc = parse("# Hello\n\nA paragraph with **bold** text.\n") doc ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ``` ::: ::: The root node is always a `DOCUMENT`. Its children are the top-level block elements. ::: {#b53252a0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} for child in doc.children: print(child) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ``` ::: ::: ## Walking the Tree The `walk()` method performs a depth-first traversal, yielding `(event, node)` pairs. Container nodes produce both `"enter"` and `"exit"` events; leaf nodes produce only `"enter"`. ::: {#8e3bb58f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} for event, node in doc.walk(): if event == "enter": print(f"{node.type_string:>15} {node.literal or ''}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` document heading text Hello paragraph text A paragraph with strong text bold text text. ``` ::: ::: This is the primary way to scan or transform a document. For example, extracting all links: ::: {#d7ee465f .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} md = "See [Python](https://python.org) and [Rust](https://rust-lang.org).\n" doc = parse(md) links = [ (node.url, node.first_child.literal) for event, node in doc.walk() if event == "enter" and node.type == NodeType.LINK ] links ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` [('https://python.org', 'Python'), ('https://rust-lang.org', 'Rust')] ``` ::: ::: ## Node Properties Each node type exposes relevant properties. Headings have a `heading_level`, links have `url` and `title`, code blocks have `fence_info`, and text nodes have `literal`. ::: {#80941579 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} doc = parse("## Installation\n\nRun `pip install multimark`.\n") for event, node in doc.walk(): if event == "enter" and node.type == NodeType.HEADING: print(f"Level {node.heading_level}: ", end="") print(node.first_child.literal) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Level 2: Installation ``` ::: ::: Source positions are available on every node: ::: {#2e018725 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} doc = parse("First paragraph.\n\nSecond paragraph.\n") for child in doc.children: print(f"Lines {child.start_line}–{child.end_line}: {child.type_string}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Lines 1–1: paragraph Lines 3–3: paragraph ``` ::: ::: ## Mutating the Tree Nodes support in-place mutation. You can change properties, add or remove nodes, and then render the modified tree. ::: {#8843e72a .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} from multimark import Node doc = parse("Visit [example](http://example.com) for details.\n") for event, node in doc.walk(): if node.type == NodeType.LINK and node.url.startswith("http://"): node.url = node.url.replace("http://", "https://", 1) print(doc.render_html()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```

Visit example for details.

``` ::: ::: You can also build nodes from scratch: ::: {#008e30f4 .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} doc = parse("Some content.\n") heading = Node.new(NodeType.HEADING) heading.heading_level = 2 text = Node.new(NodeType.TEXT) text.literal = "Table of Contents" heading.append_child(text) doc.prepend_child(heading) print(doc.render_html()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```

Table of Contents

Some content.

``` ::: ::: ## Rendering Subtrees Any node can render itself independently, which is useful for extracting fragments. ::: {#cd6e9d4b .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} doc = parse("# Title\n\nFirst paragraph.\n\nSecond paragraph.\n") second_para = list(doc.children)[2] print(second_para.render_html()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```

Second paragraph.

``` ::: ::: All six output formats are available: `render_html()`, `render_xml()`, `render_latex()`, `render_man()`, `render_commonmark()`, and `render_plaintext()`. ::: {#8f235f85 .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} print(second_para.render_plaintext()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Second paragraph. ``` ::: ::: ## Streaming Parser For large documents or streamed input, the `Parser` class provides incremental feeding. ::: {#739d3db1 .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} from multimark import Parser with Parser(smart=True) as p: p.feed("# Chapter 1\n\n") p.feed("Some text with \"quotes\" and -- dashes.\n") print(p.render_html()) print(p.render_plaintext(width=72)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```

Chapter 1

Some text with “quotes” and – dashes.

Chapter 1 Some text with “quotes” and – dashes. ``` ::: ::: The `Parser` also works as a context manager for automatic resource cleanup, and its `finish()` method returns the root `Node` for AST access: ::: {#5c024a5d .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} with Parser(extensions=["table"]) as p: p.feed("| A | B |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 2 |\n") doc = p.finish() print(doc.render_html()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ```
A B
1 2
``` ::: ::: ## GFM Extensions with the AST Extensions like tables, strikethrough, and task lists produce their own node types in the tree. These work with both `parse()` and `Parser`. ::: {#80d1af15 .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} doc = parse( "- [x] Done\n- [ ] Pending\n", extensions=["tasklist"], ) for event, node in doc.walk(): if event == "enter": print(f"{node.type_string}: {node.literal or ''}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` document: list: tasklist: paragraph: text: Done tasklist: paragraph: text: Pending ``` ::: ::: ## Common Patterns ### Extract all headings for a table of contents ::: {#1e9bf94a .cell execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} doc = parse("# Intro\n\n## Setup\n\n### Details\n\n## Usage\n") toc = [] for event, node in doc.walk(): if event == "enter" and node.type == NodeType.HEADING: level = node.heading_level text = node.first_child.literal if node.first_child else "" toc.append((level, text)) toc ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=14} ``` [(1, 'Intro'), (2, 'Setup'), (3, 'Details'), (2, 'Usage')] ``` ::: ::: ### Strip all formatting and extract plain text ::: {#cf37c243 .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} doc = parse("Hello **world**, visit [here](https://x.com).\n") texts = [ node.literal for event, node in doc.walk() if event == "enter" and node.type == NodeType.TEXT ] " ".join(texts) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=15} ``` 'Hello world , visit here .' ``` ::: ::: For comparison, render the same tree directly: ::: {#9d82c5e7 .cell execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} doc.render_plaintext() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=16} ``` 'Hello world, visit here.\n' ``` ::: ::: The manual approach collects only `TEXT` nodes and joins them with spaces. The renderer also includes code contents and preserves list markers and paragraph breaks. Some GFM markers remain, and raw HTML blocks are omitted including their text. See [Plain Text](output-formats.qmd#plain-text) for the full behavior.
